text:
jess: Heads up — GPU CI is red on main. Multiple test flakes but a consistent failure in gpu-inference-tests (runner gpu-large-12). Logs show a driver/runtime mismatch and a couple OOMs. Can someone triage? :eyes:

infra-bot: CI job gpu-inference-tests failed on runner gpu-large-12 (job id 4827). Marked flaky if rerun passes.

mike: pinging @sarah and @devops — can you grab the raw logs? also which commit?

jess: commit range is 7a3f2d2..d9b1a8f (PR #512). Attaching the tail of the failing log below:

jess: ```
[2026-03-17 09:12:34] runtime error: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/workspace/tests/run_infer.py", line 98, in <module>
    result = model.generate(input_ids, max_new_tokens=128)
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/torch/cuda/__init__.py", line 206, in _lazy_init
    raise AssertionError("Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled")
AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled

Also saw multiple OOMs earlier: 
CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 64.00 MiB (GPU 0; 15.90 GiB total capacity; 14.12 GiB already allocated; 12.25 MiB free; 14.00 GiB reserved)
```

sarah: looks like runner image probably bumped CUDA or the host driver. Did the infra team update the container base yesterday?

devops: we rolled a security patch to the host nodes last night (driver 470 -> 495) on the gpu-large pool. Containers still using CUDA 11.3 runtime images — mismatch possibility. Noticed a few non-deterministic OOMs in the past 24h too.

mike: OK that explains driver mismatch. Two actionable threads: 1) short-term rerun/pin a compatible runner or downgrade driver; 2) bisect to see if our changes in PR triggered different memory patterns. Who can run a bisect?

jess: I can bisect. Quick question: what's the exact command to run the CI job locally with the same docker image and env so I can reproduce OOMs?

ci-bot: Local reproducer: 
```bash
# spin up the same job container image and mount workspace
docker run --gpus all -v $PWD:/workspace -w /workspace redwood/gpu-test-image:cuda11.3-pt2.1 /bin/bash -c "python -u tests/run_infer.py --batch 1"
# also set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 to mimic single-GPU CI
```

sarah: if it's driver/runtime mismatch, the local docker run will still use host driver. Use the image with compatible CUDA runtime (or use our gpu-compat image). Try redwood/gpu-test-image:gpu-compat-11.3 — that one carries compatibility shims we added.

jess: trying local run now, will report back.

[~12 minutes later]

jess: Quick update — local run reproduces the "driver version is insufficient" error even with gpu-compat image. Host here has driver 495, GPU runtime 11.3 -> incompatible. On CI, host update happened after our image builds. For short term I reran the CI job on a different pool (gpu-large-stable) and it passed.

mike: good catch. For long term we should either: a) pin host driver versions in infra and coordinate driver rollouts with container runtime builds, or b) rebuild our images to match host driver (and add CI smoke that checks nvidia-smi and cuda version at job start).

devops: I can rollback driver on a small subset to validate. But safer: rebuild images with newer CUDA runtime (11.8 or 12.x) and mark them with a tag that matches driver major version. Also we should add a CI guard: at job startup run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv` and `python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda)"` and fail fast with clear diagnostics.

mike: agree. Also the OOMs may be unrelated but could be exacerbated by different kernels. Jess, for bisect please run `git bisect` between 7a3f2d2 and d9b1a8f and run the CI job script locally for each step. Example:

mike: ```bash
git bisect start d9b1a8f 7a3f2d2
git bisect run ./ci/run_gpu_tests.sh --local-repro
```

jess: starting bisect now. ETA ~30-40m. I'll update thread with the culprit commit if it turns up. :mag: 

[~45 minutes later]

jess: bisect done — commit 8f4c1a9 introduced minor memory change in attention kernel (switch to fused ops). That commit increases peak memory by ~200MB in local runs and caused OOM in CI with smaller headroom.

sarah: nice find. So two simultaneous problems: driver/runtime mismatch and a higher memory regression.

devops: plan: 1) pin gpu pool selection for the release to gpu-large-stable until images are rebuilt, 2) schedule image rebuilds to CUDA 11.8 and add guard script, 3) open PR to revert or optimize 8f4c1a9 or add explicit memory-reduction fallback (config param). I'll create infra tickets.

jess: created PR #524 to limit fused attention batch size as a quick mitigation, and opened infra ticket INF-827 to rebuild images and add the guard. Rerun on gpu-large-stable passed all tests. Marking this thread resolved for now. :white_check_mark:

mike: thanks everyone — let's sync on this in the weekly infra/rls standup.

devops: noted. I'll post the rollout plan in #eng-infra. :calendar:
